thread:
anna: CI perf alarm for short-seq inference latency on nightly canary. Traces show a ~45% tail increase since last green. :eyes:
ci-bot: perf-alert: job=canary-shortseq threshold=30% exceeded (latency +45%). See https://perf.redwood/example-dashboard/shortseq
kevin: seeing it locally on a100-40gb too. Small batches (1-4), seq=16. Mean fine, p99 blowup.
ash: is this after the autobatching refactor merge? that landed yesterday right?
anna: autobatching refactor merged + triton submodule bump to 2.3.1 in the release candidate. Both landed in same window. Bisect started.
ash: try running the shortseq micro-bench: 
```
python infra/bench/shortseq.py --model rti-small --batch-sizes 1 2 4 --seq-len 16 --device cuda --triton
```
kevin: ran that; attached flamegraphs in the perf dashboard. Kernel selection flipped from fused_attn_16x64 to generic_matmul_8x32 for many calls. Memory traffic up.
ash: interesting, fused_attn was much faster on 16. Something in kernel-dispatch hints lost the fused path.
ash: can you paste the autotune table diff?
kevin: here - excerpt from triton autotune hints: 
```
- fused_attn: priority=900
+ fused_attn: priority=200
```
kevin: it looks like the bump included a heuristic change that deprioritized the fused kernel for small sequences.
ash: that would explain p99. Fused kernel has better L2 locality for small KV sizes.
ash: as a quick mitigation can we force kernel preference back for shortseq routing?
ash: add a runtime override ``--prefer-kernel fused_attn`` on canary?
anna: tried that on staging, latency goes back to normal. But rollout controls won't let us modify customer-facing production without PR and review. This is a rollout blocker.
ci-bot: perf-bisect started: suspected commits: infra/autobatch-refactor@f12d3, submods/triton@2.3.1-bump
ash: do a git bisect across our repo first (include submodule changes) to confirm which one.
kevin: git bisect narrowed to submods/triton bump. Confirmed by checking the same commit with old triton built: green.
kevin: attaching a short diff from triton that changed kernel hint ordering and matmul tiling thresholds.
ash: file an internal issue and request a revert or a patch to restore fused_attn priority for seq<=32.
anna: made an internal ticket: PERF-8943 "triton 2.3.1 heuristic flip causes fused_attn deprioritization -> p99 spikes" and flagged as P0 rollout-blocker.
ash: great. Is there a minimal patch we can apply in our runtime to remap the hint without reverting triton? e.g., override autotune table on load?
kevin: yes, we can ship a hotfix that injects a small JSON autotune override at model load. I tested locally; p99 back to baseline. Patch is tiny.
maria: can we push that to canary as emergency fix and run 2-hour soak?
anna: ops: we can push hotfix to canary in ~30m, but need approvals for prod.
sre-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 1959623800, monitoring alerts on.
ash: also notify Triton upstream. We shouldn't maintain long-term patches if they change heuristics unexpectedly.
kevin: opened upstream issue: https://github.com/triton-inference-server/issues/12345 with perf traces and autotune diff.
ash: action items: 1) push runtime hotfix to override fused_attn priority for seq<=32 (kevin) 2) canary deploy + soak (anna/sre) 3) upstream issue and request reversible change (kevin) 4) prepare revert PR for release branch if hotfix fails (ashok).
ash: timeline: if canary fails after hotfix, revert the triton bump in release within 2 hours.
anna: deploying hotfix to canary now. Will post results in 15m.
kevin: scrubbed perf dash after hotfix; p99 back within 3% of baseline for the shortseq test.
anna: canary soak 15m passed, increasing to 2h.
ash: nice work. We should add a regression test that covers fused vs generic kernel choices for short sequences on A100 to catch this in CI.
kevin: opened internal PR for a microbench test and a check that fused_attn remains preferred for seq<=32 on our perf matrix.
anna: leaving this thread pinned until prod rollout clear. Thanks all :party:
